goal: Close the phase-aware Assurance deadline cutover after the terminal-receipt repair exhausted its Review follow-up limit, requiring standard Agent settlement to use only a host-created validated terminal receipt.

acceptance.assertion: Native Review preparation, standard Agent dispatch, workload-classified execution, and verdict validation use independent budgets; quick, standard, and heavy profiles derive only from the frozen intent risk and immutable bundle; soft expiry remains nonterminal and accepts a later matching fresh verdict; the former 300-second end-to-end deadline and heartbeat-free stalled state are absent.

Review stop thresholds and explicit cancellation enter nonterminal fail-closed settlement; standard Agent and injected handles treat stop acknowledgement, local promise resolution or rejection, elapsed time, and nonterminal get_subagent_result payloads as non-authoritative; both paths use host-created deferred receipts resolved or rejected only after matching agent identity, reserved operation provenance, and validated native terminal status from get_subagent_result; handle.result is advisory-only and is never assigned as the terminal receipt; evidence deletion and terminal follow-up require a branded native_terminal outcome; startup and dispatch-timeout late handles never fall back to local result; helper rejection retains settlement ownership and evidence; late or conflicting results perform zero authority writes; and exactly one terminal follow-up wins for each task, operation, and role across completion, startup stop, cancel, failure, and same-tick races.

Deterministic QA derives one aggregate deadline from the sequential verification descriptor timeouts plus bounded overhead, retains the fifteen-minute floor and sixty-minute ceiling, rejects an impossible declared aggregate before immutable snapshot capture or the first verification, and projects the derived value consistently without weakening each descriptor timeout or authority-commit linearization.

Source, Pi extension exports, focused contracts, protocol documentation, source Skill, and packaged Skill describe the same phase-aware budgets, workload profiles, waiting-user semantics, terminal ownership, and deferred cross-session persistence boundary with no active five-second startup or 300-second end-to-end Review contract.
The complete Pi extension graph passes strict TypeScript checking and the full repository test suite passes after the timing-policy cutover.
